workflows:abort.description: Abort an in-flight workflow instance — a hard stop: pending effects are cancelled, stage guards removed, and the instance is marked terminal where it stands.
examples: <%= config.bin %> workflows abort wf-instance.abc123 --reason 'superseded by relaunch'

deployment.description: Deployment name — narrow the instance search to the resource that deployment targets; the tag partition still comes from the loaded instance.
deployment.name: deployment

tag.description: Workflow environment tag (e.g. prod, test) — an optional query filter that also narrows which resources are searched; omit to span them all.
tag.name: tag

workflows:deploy.description: Validate, diff, and deploy workflow definitions to the resource bound by the selected deployment.

deployment.description: Deployment name — the unique identity of one deployment in the config.
deployment.name: deployment

tag.description: Workflow environment tag (e.g. prod, test) — deploys every deployment carrying the tag (a tag is an environment group).
tag.name: tag

all-tags.description: Deploy every deployment in the config, not just a selection.
all-tags.name: all-tags

dry-run.description: Validate + diff against the deployed version; do not write.
dry-run.name: dry-run

check.description: Validate definitions only; do not contact the dataset.
check.name: check

only.description: Limit deploy/check/diff to a single workflow definition by name (deployments are selected with --deployment). Every targeted deployment must contain it.
only.name: only

share-defs.description: Share the definition documents newly created by this deploy with Sanity — the full document, verbatim (structure, names, filters, effect configuration, seeded values), plus its deployment coordinates (project and dataset, or resource id); never content documents, instances, or your Sanity auth token. Sharing is the default in every environment, including CI / non-TTY / DO_NOT_TRACK. Use --no-share-defs to opt out.
share-defs.name: share-defs

workflows:diagnose.description: Explain why a workflow instance is or isn't progressing, and what would unstick it.

workflows:fire-action.description: Fire an action on an instance to unstick a waiting activity — the write acts as the configured token. Omit --action to list what can be fired.
examples: <%= config.bin %> workflows fire-action wf-instance.abc123 --activity approve --action approve
<%= config.bin %> workflows fire-action wf-instance.abc123 --activity publish --action publish --param note=shipping

workflows:nuke.description: The reset for a dataset holding engine documents the versioned upgrade framework cannot yet migrate: deletes the tag's instances, definitions, and guards (across every alias-bound resource). --instance <id> instead deletes one terminal instance plus its guards. Content documents are never touched. Prints a dry-run plan, then confirms (--force skips the prompt; the plan still prints).

deployment.description: The deployment name to reset. With --instance, narrows which deployment the instance is looked up in when its tag spans several.
deployment.name: deployment

tag.description: The deployment tag to reset (while it names exactly one deployment). Not valid with --instance, which reads its tag from the instance id.
tag.name: tag

instance.description: Delete a single terminal instance by id, plus its guard docs, instead of a tag.
instance.name: instance

force.description: Skip the confirmation prompt (for scripts/CI). The plan still prints.
force.name: force

workflows:nuke.summary: Delete engine-owned documents — a whole deployment tag, or a single instance.

activity.description: Activity name within the current stage.
activity.name: activity

workflows:reset-activity.description: Reset a failed activity on an in-flight instance — back to active to re-run it, or --skip to bypass it (mark it skipped) so a gated exit transition can fire.

tag.name: tag

skip.description: Bypass the activity (mark it skipped) instead of re-running it (back to active).
skip.name: skip

workflows:set-stage.description: Force an instance into a stage, regardless of its declared transitions and filters — the engine's setStage admin override. The target stage's enter lifecycle still runs (auto-activities start, stage guards reconcile), and the post-move cascade can immediately auto-transition the instance onward.
examples: <%= config.bin %> workflows set-stage wf-instance.abc123 --to ready --reason 'unblock for demo'
